previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and chronic left index finger wound due to steal syndrome was admitted with worsening pain, fevers, and signs of infection. Imaging revealed osteomyelitis and soft tissue infection, leading to a left index finger ray amputation and tendon transfer. Blood and wound cultures grew E. coli, sensitive to ertapenem. He was treated with IV antibiotics, initially meropenem, and transitioned to outpatient IV ertapenem via a PICC line for a six-week course. His acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and his blood pressure and glucose levels were managed with continued home medications. The patient improved clinically, with a clean incision and stable vitals, and was discharged home with wound care instructions, pain management, and follow-up plans with hand surgery and infectious disease.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Right toe infection.  

COMPARISON:  Comparison made with right foot radiographs from ___.  

FINDINGS:  Right foot, 3 views.  Prior amputations of multiple toes are seen. 
Patchy demineralization involving the bones of the ___ toe limits evaluation
for subtle osteomyelitis.  Diffuse soft tissue edema is seen, but no
subcutaneous air or discrete foreign body.  Vascular calcifications and
diffuse soft tissue edema is seen throughout the foot.  No acute fracture or
dislocation is seen.  

IMPRESSION:  Diffuse soft tissue edema.  Demineralization in the ___ toe is
progressed which limits evaluation for subtle acute osteomyelitis.

RESTING LOWER ARTERIAL DOPPLER STUDY

HISTORY:  Gangrenous right fourth toe, left popliteal to DP bypass graft,
status post right first to third toe amputations.

FINDINGS:  ABIs, Doppler waveforms and PVRs were obtained bilaterally at rest
only.  

RIGHT LEG:  The ABI of the posterior tibial is 1.07; however, significance of
this finding is uncertain as the vessels are non-compressible.  No digital
measurement could be obtained on this side.  Doppler waveforms were triphasic
in the femoral and popliteal region but monophasic in the posterior tibial and
dorsalis pedis.  PVR waveforms are likely depressed in the lower leg.

LEFT LEG:  Only a digital ABI could be obtained at 0.52.  Doppler waveforms
are triphasic in the femoral and popliteal region, monophasic below this. 
PVRs are moderately depressed at the metatarsal level.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Essentially satisfactory inflow up to the level of the popliteal arteries.
2.  Status post popliteal to DP bypass graft.
3.  Right tibial disease.

INDICATION:  Fourth toe infection status post amputation.

TECHNIQUE:  Three views, right foot.

COMPARISON:  Right foot radiograph; ___.

FINDINGS:

There has been interval resection of the fourth ray at the level of the
proximal phalanx.  Prior resections of the other toes with amputation of the
first toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint, second toe at the proximal
phalanx, third toe at the proximal phalanx.  No resection of the fifth toe
evident.  Extensive vascular calcifications.  No fracture or dislocation seen.
Mild osteopenia at the level of the metatarsal heads.  No convincing evidence
of residual osteomyelitis.  Small enthesophyte at the Achilles tendon
insertion.  Degenerative change at the talonaviular joint.  Diffuse soft
tissue swelling.

IMPRESSION:  Status post resection of the fourth toe at the level of the
proximal phalanx.  No convincing radiographic evidence for acute
osteomyelitis.
